title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md follows the standard wai template. Missing: all Layer 3 patterns (Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint, drift detection).

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

### References
- agent-value-alignment skill: references/layer-3-runtime-prompt.md
- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)

title: doctor orphan-contract suppression misses rev-18 VERIFIES ids (80 false orphans)
description:
## Why this exists

`ah doctor` emits 80 false `orphan-contract` failures on this repo (exit 1)
since the rev-18 dogfood rekey (7b2311c, 2026-10-08): the OrphanContractCheck
suppression parses scenario VERIFIES bullets as the literal legacy shape
`- **VERIFIES** [[spec.P-x]]` (src/doctor.rs:272 strip_prefix "- **VERIFIES** [[spec."),
but rev-18 trees carry real capability ids — `[[auth.tokens.P-x]]`,
`[[lint.P-vague]]`, etc. So `linked_contract_ids` is always empty and every
derived contract is reported as an orphan.

Verified against v0.10.0 worktree: 74 orphans pre-existing there too
(not a release regression; grew by exactly the 6 new gate contracts).
`ah check`'s equivalent suppression (src/check.rs:573) parses the correct
open-ended shape `strip_prefix("- **VERIFIES** [[")` — doctor must match it.

## What needs to be done

1. RED: unit test in src/doctor.rs — a fixture scenario carrying
   `- **VERIFIES** [[lint.P-vague]]` suppresses the orphan finding for
   contract lint/p-vague.toml (today: reported).
2. GREEN: change doctor.rs:272 to the check.rs shape:
   strip_prefix("- **VERIFIES** [[") then split on '.' — last segment is
   the property id (reuse or mirror check.rs parsing; consider extracting
   a shared helper if trivial).
3. Verify full repo: ah doctor orphan count 80 -> ~0 (any true orphan
   findings should survive), suite green.
4. Keep the sync.slugify_property_id mapping consistent with check.rs.

## Acceptance criteria

Must: ah doctor on this repo reports no orphan-contract findings for any
contract referenced by a rev-18 VERIFIES bullet; a genuinely orphaned
contract (no scenario, no VERIFIES link) still fails.
Meter: unit test above + `ah doctor --json | grep -c orphan-contracts`
drops from 80 to 0 (or to a count of true orphans).

## Anti-goals

- No behavior change to ah check's parsing (it is already correct).
- No new config or TOML fields.

title: check: overlay-conflict fires on byte-identical scenario carry-along (spec-code drift)
description:
Spec-code drift found by running `ah check --changes batch-runner-spawns` (bm2 design lane, 2026-10-10).

**Spec** (openspec/specs/gate/spec.md, Change Overlay Scope):
- "Apply modified scenario text from change overlay" — GIVEN a change delta defines a scenario that exists deployed **with different body text** AND a staged contract — THEN overlay text applies, no overlay-conflict.
- "Reject unsignaled scenario redefinition" — GIVEN a change delta defines a scenario that exists deployed **with different body text** AND no staged contract — THEN overlay-conflict.

Both scenarios pin the conflict to **different body text**. openspec's MODIFIED-requirement rule forces verbatim carry-along of unchanged scenarios into every MODIFIED delta, so byte-identical (spec,id) pairs are legitimate and must NOT conflict.

**Code** (src/check.rs:467): the `scenarios.contains_key(&key)` branch fires overlay-conflict on ANY same-id scenario without a staged contract — no body comparison. Byte-identical carry-along scenarios are flagged as conflicts: a false positive against the tool's own deployed spec.

**Repro**: ah check --changes batch-runner-spawns → 8 overlay-conflict findings for scenarios whose bodies are byte-identical to deployed (run-configured-unit-test, run-shell-test, enforce-test-timeout, capture-bounded-output-tails, missing-runner-fails-structurally, invalid-toml-syntax-fails-structurally, malformed-test-entry-fails-structurally, non-zero-declared-test-fails-check).

**Fix shape**: in the same branch, compare trimmed scenario bodies; identical body + no staged contract → silent carry-along (no finding, deployed text stands); differing body + no staged contract → overlay-conflict as today. Trailing blank lines/whitespace must not count as a difference (extract_body already normalizes trailing empties).

**Acceptance (Must + Meter)**:
- RED: `cargo test -q overlay` — new test: change delta carrying a byte-identical copy of a deployed scenario (no staged contract) emits NO overlay-conflict; current binary emits one (RED).
- GREEN: same test passes after fix; existing differing-body tests (check.rs:2336-2388 area) pass unmodified.
- Meter command: `cargo test -q overlay -- --nocapture` green including the new carry-along test.
notes: TDD: RED run_check_identical_body_carry_along_does_not_conflict (byte-identical carry-along emitted overlay-conflict); GREEN: body-equality exemption scoped to deployed_keys (cross-change duplicates stay conflicting per C-overlay-scope, both existing tests unmodified). Suite 554/0, clippy -D warnings + fmt clean, ah check 0, ah check --changes batch-runner-spawns now only the 6 expected no-toml phase-2 TODOs. GOTCHA: installed PATH ah (0.10.0) stale — verified with target/debug/ah.

title: runner: batch ah check --run-tests spawns per (runner, test file) instead of per contract (GH#40)
description:
GH#40 (cv/charly-vibes/espectacular#40): `ah check --run-tests` spawns one runner process per contract — tambor measures 603–835s per push, ~93% of pre-push gate time (658 contracts, vitest ~1s+ startup per spawn).

**Root cause** (src/runner.rs::run_declared_tests): `for entry in entries { execute_command(...) }` — one spawned runner process per contract test entry, sequential.

**Batching sketch** (from issue): group contracts by (runner, bound test file), one runner invocation per file, attribute per-contract pass/fail from the runner's structured output (vitest junit reporter emits per-test names matching the scenario-scoped `-t` patterns currently passed per spawn). `matched_zero_tests` (4.3) needs a batched equivalent: a contract whose pattern matched nothing still fails; a file run whose junit covers all bound contracts passes them individually.

**Sweep result (2026-10-10)**: same pattern audited across the charly suite —
- src/lint/bridge.rs is the only other real instance: `spk lint <file>` + `spk graph <path>` per dual-format spec (~34 spawns per `ah lint`, 17 spec files). `spk lint <dir>`/`spk graph <dir>` support single-invocation batching. Candidate follow-up ticket, ~100x smaller impact.
- wai pipeline oracles, espectacular quality tools, testaruda, dont, genesis, specodelic: no per-unit spawn hot spots. tambor test helpers spawn tsc per typing test (test-suite level, not shipped tool).

**Design Qs (phase 1 — DESIGN lane, settle in an interactive session before TDD)**:
1. Granularity: (runner, test file) groups — but cargo bindings have no file notion; need runner taxonomy (file-structured runners batch by file; process-style runners like cargo keep per-binding or batch by shared runner binary where filter semantics allow).
2. Attribution: require structured per-test output (junit) or fall back to per-contract spawn when the runner lacks a reporter?
3. matched_zero_tests batched semantics: pattern-matched-nothing still fails the contract even if the file run passed.
4. Interaction with Layer 2 testaruda pruning (v0.10.0) — pruning reduces contract count; batching reduces spawn count; keep both.

Phases: phase 1 design (lane `design` — settle Q1–Q3), phase 2 implementation (lane `afk` — TDD on src/runner.rs).

**Acceptance (Must + Meter)**:

Primary Meter (local, runnable by any fresh agent):
- Must: fixture corpus with N vitest-bound contracts sharing one test file runs exactly 1 runner invocation (assert spawn count ≤ file count; e2e test counting execute_command invocations).
- Meter command: `cargo test -q ah_check -- --nocapture` with the new spawn-counting e2e — must show ≤ 1 invocation for a single-file fixture (today: 1 per contract).

Secondary corroboration (environment-dependent, not gate-blocking):
- Must: tambor-shaped corpus (vitest per-file bindings) runs one runner invocation per bound test file, not per contract.
- Meter: tambor pre-push gate drops from ~790s baseline to order-of-magnitude lower (~65 vitest startups + execution).

Semantics:
- Must: per-contract pass/fail attribution identical to today's semantics (incl. no-tests-ran / matched-zero detection).
- Must: runner types lacking structured output keep current behavior (no semantic change for cargo/shell bindings).

Regression: full suite (535 tests baseline) + `ah check --run-tests` on the espectacular corpus must stay green; no-tests-ran guard tests in runner.rs must pass unmodified.

**Anti-goals**:
- A passing file run must NEVER cover a contract whose `-t` pattern matched nothing (reward-hack guard; keep matched-zero failing).
- Do NOT change the scenario contract format or TOML fields — batching is execution-internal only.
- Do NOT parallelize spawns in this ticket (concurrency is a separate concern; sequential batching already hits the target).
- Do NOT batch runner types without structured per-test output (cargo/shell keep per-binding spawns).

File-header criterion: src/runner.rs (reshaped) and any newly created module must carry a Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (src/check.rs header added only if touched).

Governance: contract format untouched; gate-spec execution semantics may need a companion openspec delta — check openspec/specs/gate/spec.md for wording pinning per-contract invocation before merging.

Priority: P1 (measured, user-reported).
notes:
--notes-file
PHASE 1 DESIGN DECIDED (2026-10-10, interactive session, user confirmed):
- Q1: Option B adaptive — one OR-joined batched invocation per runner type when binding count exceeds threshold; below threshold and for all ineligible bindings, per-binding spawns remain. Option A (superset run) rejected: conflicts with Layer 2 testaruda pruning; option D (identical flags) insufficient win.
- Threshold: fixed constant 8, justified from tambor measurement (~1s vitest startup per spawn; 8 spawns ≈ batched startup amortization crossover).

- Timeout: batched timeout = max(timeout_seconds) across batched entries; timed-out batch reports timed_out and falls back to per-binding spawns.
- Runners without structured reporter (cargo/shell/pytest) keep per-binding spawns per anti-goal.
- Governance: companion openspec change (MODIFIED gate "Test Runner Execution": one command, many verdicts) is a phase-2 prerequisite — opened in design lane.

title: ah check --run-tests: leverage testaruda selection underneath
description:
Evidence (October pi sessions): 362 `ah check --run-tests` calls, 673 min total, median 111.5s. ah runs ALL declared contract tests (shell, custom, property, snapshot). Meanwhile testaruda (test selection engine: select -> run -> ingest -> calibrate) is barely used outside tambor (REPLy.jl 50 ah-calls / 0 testaruda; espectacular 51/1; gently 22/3). Agents default to run-everything because that is what the tool offers.

Fix: when the project has a testaruda store initialized, `ah check --run-tests` routes declared contract tests through `testaruda select` and executes only the affected set; escape hatch `--all-tests` for full runs; exit 20 (nothing affected) maps to a benign pass-through. Secondary: single-pass output so agents stop running the --json variant and a tail variant back-to-back (observed repeatedly).

TDD: red = integration test: seeded testaruda store + changed file -> ah check --run-tests runs only selected contract tests and reports selection in JSON; green = implement; refactor = unify with existing test-runner plumbing.
notes:
Investigation (2026-10-09, 1076 pi sessions): ticket evidence validated (478 --run-tests all-time/676min; p50=2s p90=167s). Pain is the TAIL: tambor TS/npm 79 calls->176min, wanna 148->160min. NOT validated: json+tail double-run (0 pairs found) — deprioritize single-pass output. KEY REVISION: 'store initialized' gate forfeits most of the win (heaviest ah users have no testaruda store). Layered design: L1 always-on language-agnostic capability selection inside ah (changed files->spec->scenario->contract via 1:1 spec-TOML provenance); L2 testaruda select --files refinement only when store exists (filter injection via TestEntry.flags/compose_command). EXIT 20 CORRECTION: EMPTY = no code affected -> skip L2 only, still run L1 spec-side selection (spec change must verify own contracts; avoid false green). TDD red: (a) changed spec file -> only that capability's contracts run, selection in JSON; (b) seeded store + changed code file -> pruned set + --all-tests escape hatch. Research: .wai/resources/reflections/ah-run-tests-selection-research.org

Selection reported in JSON ({selected:[capability],skipped:N,source:spec-provenance}). Conservative fallback: changed set mapping to no capability -> run-all. Smoke test in this repo: selects lint (32 contracts) and skips 192 scenarios. 4 new integration tests, 542 pass, 0 warnings. title: ah check binary never emits slug-collision for deployed specs (BTreeMap collapse in resolve_scope)
description:
Discovered during espectacular-cgt (2026-10-03), out of scope, deferred.

## Problem
`resolve_scope` (src/check.rs ~L170) collapses base_scenarios into a
BTreeMap keyed (spec_path, id) — same-key duplicates are silently dropped
(last wins). `collect_structural_findings` then runs
`openspec::detect_slug_collisions` over the collapsed vec, so every key is
unique and the slug-collision finding NEVER fires from the `ah check`
binary on deployed specs. Change-overlay added_scenarios collapse the same
way in the merge loop.

The `structural_findings()` helper (doctor path) passes the raw discovery
list and DOES flag collisions — so the kind is unit-true but
binary-stale: only structural_findings()/doctor see them. History:
c96615a made parse pass both colliding scenarios through; f358e3e's
BTreeMap collapse eats them before detection.

## Fix shape
Detect collisions on the raw scenario lists (base + per-change added)
BEFORE the map collapse, push structural_report findings into
scope.findings. Keep map collapse semantics unchanged (last wins) for
downstream processing.

## Acceptance
Must: `ah check` binary emits slug-collision findings for a deployed
fixture with two same-id/different-body scenarios (and for staged
scenarios colliding within one change); existing four-findings/doctor
fixtures stay green; ah check on the real corpus stays 0.
Meter: RED integration test through resolve_scope/check binary first,
then GREEN; full suite + clippy -D warnings + ah check clean.
notes:
files touched per convention
Fixed in fcfead1: slug_collision_findings helper detects on raw base discovery before the (spec,id) BTreeMap collapse; map semantics unchanged. Scope decision: change-overlay staged-vs-staged same-id pairs already surface as overlay-conflict (a finding does fire there), so only the deployed-spec path was dead — no change-loop detection added. RED check-binary test ah_check_emits_slug_collision_for_deployed_specs; suite green, clippy -D warnings/fmt/specodelic-gates/ah check clean, real corpus 0 findings, ah check --run-tests 227/0. title: ah init wires ah-check outside lefthook commands: — flip wrongly-pinned init_cli.rs test after genesis-r99 fix (GH#31)
description:
**Source:** charly-vibes/espectacular#31 (sk/REPLy.jl, verified live on ah 0.9.0)

`ah init`'s lefthook managed block lands directly after the stage key (`pre-commit:`), so `ah-check` becomes a sibling of `commands:`. Lefthook 1.13.6 silently ignores stage-level `ah-check` at runtime (only `lefthook validate` rejects it) — **the wire is a silent no-op**.

Fixed already: glued markers (3be5214), duplicates on re-run (idempotent — verified).
Still live: placement outside `commands:`.

Root cause is genesis-side (genesis-r99: `ensure_wired` spec mandates "directly after `pre-commit:`"). This ticket is the downstream half: once genesis ships the fix and the pin is bumped, flip the wrongly-pinned test and pin correct nesting.

Steps:
1. Bump genesis-vibes pin to the release carrying genesis-r99 (check crates.io).
2. Flip `tests/init_cli.rs` assertion "block must land directly after the column-0 pre-commit anchor" → block nested inside `commands:` (4-space indent on ah-check under commands:).
3. e2e with real lefthook in tempdir: `lefthook validate` passes, `git commit` actually runs `ah check`.
4. Update stale comments in src/init.rs (LEFTHOOK_AH_COMMAND doc + line ~533 "land under the column-0 pre-commit anchor").
5. Comment resolution on GH#31 (keep open until reporter confirms or close with fix version).

TDD: write the flipped pin RED against current genesis first (it will fail — placement is stage-level), then make it GREEN with the pin bump. The RED test doubles as the downstream contract for genesis-r99.
acceptance_criteria: init_cli.rs pins ah-check nested inside commands:; real-lefthook e2e: validate passes + ah check runs on commit; genesis pin bumped to release carrying genesis-r99; GH#31 resolved
notes:
Root cause tracked genesis-side as genesis-r99 (separate bd database — no cross-repo dep possible). Sequence: genesis-r99 fix+release → this ticket.
genesis 0.12.0 released (genesis-r99); espectacular 1653eae: pin bump + LEFTHOOK_AH_COMMAND inner form + init_cli.rs pin flipped; e2e verified (lefthook validate passes, ah-check runs on commit, idempotent); GH#31 commented, close after next ah release ships the fix

title: ah check: bare ENOENT fail-closed when specs dir doesn't exist (GH#28.2)
description:
Reported in ah 0.8.0 (GH#28 item 2; 0.3.0 returned "no issues — 0 structural" on the same tree). With [paths] specs = "openspec/specs" pointing at a not-yet-created dir (repo has only openspec/changes/), ah check dies with a bare "ah: No such file or directory (os error 2)" — no path in the message, so a lefthook commit gate went red with nothing actionable (reporter lost an hour).

title: ah init: false 'unanchorable stage key' on plain lefthook.yml with preceding comments (GH#28.1)
description: Reported in ah 0.8.0 against a babashka/hledger repo (GH#28, item 1; worked on 0.3.0). ah init aborts with "cannot anchor stage 'pre-commit' in lefthook.yml: stage key is quoted or otherwise not anchorable at column 0" even though the file has a clean unquoted column-0 pre-commit: key — the file merely starts with comment lines. title: Tracer bullet: one dont rejection signal end-to-end through espectacular to wai
description:
Prove the feedback loop works for one concrete signal before generalizing. This ticket cuts vertically through dont → espectacular → wai:

1. **dont** emits one structured rejection event (e.g., ungrounded-claim rule fires) as JSON to a known location
2. **espectacular** reads the event, maps it to an openspec assertion, and produces a drift signal
3. **wai** consumes the drift signal and surfaces it during wai status or wai doctor

## Done criteria

- A working demo: run dont on a file with an ungrounded claim → espectacular picks up the rejection → wai doctor shows a drift warning
- The event schema is documented (even if minimal)
- Each tool's integration point is a single function behind a feature flag

## Scope constraints

- One signal type only (ungrounded-claim rejection from dont)
- One language only (Go or Rust — whichever has an existing openspec scenario to test against)
- No persistence layer — file-based events are sufficient for the tracer bullet
- No CI integration yet

## Starting points

- **dont:** src/envelope.rs:72-105 (ErrorResult struct) — extend to optionally write a structured event file
- **espectacular:** new — minimal binary that reads an event file and emits a drift signal
- **wai:** src/commands/doctor.rs:2100-2180 (artifact lock checks) — extend to also check for espectacular drift signals

## Downstream

Once this works, the three generalization tickets become unblocked:
- dont-nwck — generalize rejection event capture
- pretender-5rk — add pretender violation events to the same pipeline
- wai-f0dv — generalize drift consumption beyond espectacular signals

title: Contract TOML guidance: no pattern for scenario-scoped test commands — file-level includes re-run whole suites per contract (GH#32)
description:
**Source:** charly-vibes/espectacular#32 (sk/REPLy.jl, ~36 contracts across 4 specs)

No documented/pattern-supported way to write **scenario-scoped** test commands in contract TOMLs. The natural authoring pattern — `[[tests.shell]]` with an `include` of the whole test file containing the scenario's assertions — re-executes the entire file for every contract that maps to any scenario in it.

Consequences reported: `ah check --run-tests` runs the same suite once per contract (N× wall time), failure attribution blurs across scenarios, and authors are forced into either correctness (whole-file include) or speed (per-scenario duplication by hand).

Scope to explore (decide, don't assume):

The two halves of the suite are disjoint in integration design: when vampiro/crua/livin ship, there is no specced path for their findings to surface in 'ah check' output.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add optional config blocks mirroring the existing pattern:
  [quality.composability]
  enabled = true
  command = [...]   # vampiro check producing a JSON envelope
  [quality.cost]
  enabled = true
  command = [...]   # crua check
  [quality.boundary-coverage]
  enabled = true
  command = [...]   # livin check
- Define new finding kinds: quality-composability, quality-cost, quality-boundary-coverage in schemas/check-output.schema.json and the finding-kinds table.
- Like the existing quality-* signals, these are informational (do not cause ah check to exit non-zero).
- Reuse the custom-runner JSON envelope protocol so the trio only needs to emit {exit_code, passed, findings}.
- Document in README that these signals consume the trio when installed, and that absence is fine (graceful no-op).

title: Draw the mutation-testing boundary vs pretender (scoring ownership)
description:
Finding M6 from the charly suite consistency evaluation.

Mutation testing is touched by two suite tools:
- 'pretender mutation' wraps cargo-mutants / mutmut / Stryker / PIT and reports scores.
- espectacular's [quality.mutation] also runs mutation (via a command template) and emits a quality-mutation finding.

In a repo that wires both, the same mutation run can be invoked twice, or scored against two different thresholds (pretender's band config vs espectacular's quality.mutation.threshold), with no documented owner.

This is a decision ticket: pick the ownership boundary.

Options:
A) pretender owns mutation execution + scoring; espectacular's quality.mutation reads pretender's report (custom-runner envelope) rather than re-running. Remove the command template from espectacular; keep only 'command = pretender mutation --format json' style.
B) espectacular owns mutation scoring as a quality signal; pretender drops the 'pretender mutation' subcommand and only documents how to run mutators (no scoring).
C) Keep both but document a clear non-overlap: pretender.mutation is the runner/wrapper; espectacular.quality.mutation is the gate threshold. State that only one should be wired per repo.

Acceptance criteria:
- A decision recorded in both espectacular README and pretender docs.
- The non-chosen path is deprecated or scoped in docs.
- If C, add a 'pretender doctor'/'ah doctor' warning when both are configured in one repo.
notes: DECISION RECORDED: Option A — pretender owns mutation execution + scoring; espectacular's quality.mutation consumes pretender's report (custom-runner envelope). Basis: Jev System One judgment (jev-1.13.0) — choice A @ 0.91 probability (B 0.03, C 0.06), confidence 0.86; problem-is-real 0.92; consume-over-rerun 0.88; narrowed doctor warning kept per 0.64 nuance. Implemented espectacular side: README records decision + deprecates raw-mutator and {}-template wiring; new mutation-ownership doctor check warns only on raw-mutator commands (cargo-mutants/mutmut/stryker/pit); mu5 ['{}'] default stays warning-free. pretender-side doc recording remains open (other repo).

title: Runner should treat zero-tests-matched as contract failure
description:
## Why this exists

When a [[tests.shell]] command uses a cargo test filter that matches no tests (e.g. due to a renamed or deleted test function), cargo test -q exits 0 with '0 tests run'. espectacular interprets exit 0 as PASSED, so the contract silently becomes green with no tests actually executed. This breaks the monitoring guarantee: the contract appears wired but exercises nothing.

## What needs to be done

In the shell test runner (likely src/runner.rs or wherever shell test results are collected), after a test command exits 0, check whether any tests actually ran. If 0 tests ran but exit was 0, emit a new finding kind (e.g. no-tests-ran or test-filter-matched-nothing) rather than treating the contract as passing.

This requires parsing the cargo test -q output line 'test result: ok. N passed' and treating N=0 with exit 0 as a failure condition.

## Acceptance criteria

- ah check emits a finding (not silent pass) when a [[tests.shell]] command exits 0 but runs 0 tests
- Existing contracts with real tests continue to pass normally
- The finding kind is documented in ah explain
close_reason: Implemented: shell tests that exit 0 with cargo-style '0 passed' output now emit no-tests-ran finding; added explain topic; 3 tests cover zero/nonzero/plain-exit cases

title: ah scenario new creates stubs that immediately fail ah check
description:
## Why this exists

When ah scenario new creates a contract stub, the generated .toml does not include a [[tests.*]] entry. Because the Contract struct requires tests (no #[serde(default)]), every stub immediately fails ah check with malformed-contract.

This creates a poor workflow: you run ah scenario new, then run ah check out of habit, and get 81 errors — all noise, none of them actionable without knowing the schema.

## What needs to be done

Option A: Add a placeholder [[tests.shell]] comment or empty section to generated stubs so the schema is valid from creation.

title: malformed-contract error message misleads: says 'invalid TOML' when field is missing
description:
## Why this exists

When a contract file is syntactically valid TOML but missing the required tests field, ah check reports:
  'invalid TOML in /path/to/contract.toml'

This is misleading — the TOML is perfectly valid. The real error is a missing required field.

The root cause is in src/contracts.rs:28 where toml::from_str uses a generic context message:
  .with_context(|| format!("invalid TOML in {toml_path}"))

When serde fails to deserialize (missing field, wrong type, etc.), the context swallows the real error.

Additionally, the playbook guidance for malformed-contract says 'fix the invalid field in the .toml' without identifying which field is wrong, leaving the user to guess.

## What needs to be done

1. In load_contract(), propagate the actual deserialization error (e.g. 'missing field tests') instead of overwriting it with 'invalid TOML in ...'
2. In the malformed-contract playbook entry (explain/), add guidance: 'run ah check --verbose or inspect the error message to identify the missing/invalid field'
3. Consider emitting the specific field name in the finding message field

## Acceptance criteria

When a contract is missing the tests field, ah check message field reads something like:
  'contract missing required field: tests (in path/to/contract.toml)'
rather than the generic 'invalid TOML in ...'.
notes: The malformed-contract explain topic is in src/explain.rs (static MALFORMED_CONTRACT around line 419). The review_and_apply topic at ~line 775 also references malformed-contract and needs updating. Both were updated as part of the 2026-06-18 fix.

title: ah Q6: custom runner plugin protocol
description:
Section 6 + Section 0 of add-quality-measurement-and-adapters (tasks.md 0.1–0.5, 6.1–6.5).

Absorbs the Q0 envelope schema (formerly 6nm.1, folded in per review: the envelope is consumed only by the custom runner plugin, so coupling it here keeps schema and consumer in one ticket).

Covers:
- Author schemas/custom-runner.schema.json (envelope: exit_code int required, passed bool required, findings array required; empty findings + exit_code 0 is valid pass)
- Cross-reference from schemas/check-output.schema.json so finding object definition is shared
- Custom adapter (runner = '\''custom'\'') invokes a user-defined executable
- Validate envelope against the schema; map structural violations to envelope_violation findings (test-failing)
- Capture stderr in execution_error findings when the runner exits non-zero
design:
Why fold envelope schema here (formerly Q0 / 6nm.1):
- The envelope is consumed ONLY by the custom runner plugin. Defining it in a separate horizontal-layer ticket created a false 'blocks Q3–Q6' dependency.
- Q3 (pytest), Q4 (cargo), Q5 (vitest) speak their toolchain's native protocol, not the custom envelope.
- Schema-and-consumer in one ticket means one PR ships a working capability, not two PRs that only work together.

Envelope shape rationale:
- exit_code (int, required) — Unix convention; lets shell-only consumers gate without parsing JSON.
- passed (bool, required) — denormalizes the success signal so the gate doesn't infer from exit_code alone; lets runners report 'all tests ran but findings present' (exit 0, passed false).
- findings (array, required) — empty array on green so the schema is always uniform; uses the same finding object as schemas/check-output.schema.json via JSON Schema $ref.

Alternatives considered:
- Native protocol per runner (no envelope) — rejected: forces every custom runner author to re-derive the same translation layer.
- Wrap stdout as text with markers — rejected: not deterministic, brittle to runner stderr/stdout interleaving.
acceptance_criteria: schemas/custom-runner.schema.json validates as JSON Schema; ah check with runner='custom' invokes the configured executable, parses the envelope (exit_code, passed, findings), and validates structurally; empty findings + exit_code 0 is a valid pass; non-zero exit captures stderr in execution_error findings; envelope-shape violations emit envelope_violation findings.

title: Audit 56 passing contracts for correct test filter scope
description:
## Why this exists

ah check reports 56 contracts as passing, but a green contract only proves the declared test command exits zero — not that the test filter actually targets the right behavior. A filter like 'cargo test -q ah_archive_' covers all archive tests regardless of the specific scenario; if future tests are added nearby, a contract could stay green while covering unintended tests.

## What needs to be done

For each passing contract, verify that the test filter (flags/command) is as narrow as possible and actually exercises the scenario named in the contract. Cross-reference the scenario prose with the test body.

## Acceptance criteria

Each passing contract's test filter can be justified by pointing to specific test functions or test names that correspond to the scenario.
